rows.title: Cellular memory of acquired stress resistance in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
rows.snippet: Cells with prior NaCl exposure have a faster gene-expression response to H2O2.
rows.qualification: Guan et al. 2012, PMID:22851651, PMC3454879; complete opening sentence of the Figure 4 caption, contiguous in publisher HTML with chemical subscripts retained as text. BY4741-background laboratory yeast received 0.7 M NaCl for 60 minutes, washing and 240 minutes of stress-free YPD recovery (two generations in Results), then 0.5 mM H2O2, compared with mock-treated cells. No significant pre-challenge expression difference at FDR 0.05 does not prove identical baselines. Figure 4 includes induced and repressed genes; only the enhanced-induction subset supports this activation phenotype. The 449-gene count is not a count of induced genes. Methods and Figure 4A sample through 40 minutes, whereas Results describes a 60-minute response. Figure 5 shows TSA2 mRNA kinetics by qPCR; nup42 deletion reduces the priming benefit, while nup100 naive and primed responses are both fast, not simple evidence of a universal mechanism. Four-to-five generation resistance persistence is a different endpoint. Relevant Results, Methods, scientific abstract and actual Figures 4 and 5 were inspected; raw data were not reanalyzed. Native abstract-verifier results are retained separately in the source sidecar; exact publisher full-text matching supports this caption quotation.

curation_decision.label: enhanced transcriptional reactivation memory
curation_decision.definition: A physiological phenotype in which a microbial cell or lineage retains a non-genetic state from prior inducing conditions that enhances the rate or magnitude of later transcriptional activation after intervening repression.
curation_decision.identity_decision: Positive assay-defined phenotype accepted independently, not inferred from deprecated labels. No exact active record in the inspected scope. Historical original definitions for METPO:1000108 and METPO:1000310 remain unresolved, with reason assignment disputed in METPO#521. No revival, exact synonym or equivalence xref is asserted.
curation_decision.evidence_limits: Same research lineage, not independent laboratories. INO1 enhancement uses synthetic Opi1 Anchor Away; ordinary starvation reactivation is not clearly faster. Selected transcript measurements do not directly measure initiation rate or universally establish inheritance, molecular mechanism or duration. D'Urso Figure 7A tests two-hour recovery; its four-generation sentence attributes prior Guan evidence. Preserve figure/caption and supplement discrepancies.

rows.qualification: D'Urso et al. 2016, PMID:27336723, PMC4951200; Results s2-7, paragraph 1, contiguous in primary XML and publisher Version of Record HTML. This complete sentence reports the authors' own confirmation: prior salt exposure enhances later peroxide-induced mRNA responses. The preceding sentence attributes the gene count and duration to Guan 2012, not a new measurement here. Figure 7A directly tests selected mRNA responses after 0.7 M NaCl for one hour, two-hour rich-medium recovery, then 0.5 mM H2O2. PGM2, PMT5 and YGP1 differ from the HSP31 control; USV1 is explicitly not shown. Four-generation persistence is not measured in that panel. Actual Figure 7B is wild-type ChIP, C mutant ChIP, D mutant mRNA and E Ssn3 ChIP; caption B/C/D assignments conflict with the image. INO1 mutant reactivation defects in Figure 1E/F alone do not establish faster within-wild-type reactivation. Relevant Results, Methods, abstract and actual figures were inspected; raw data were not reanalyzed. Native abstract lookup returns NOT_IN_ABSTRACT, with the selected quotation independently matched in full text.
